scope:
Training-only leave-engine-out ridge probes of fixed lexical embeddings.

These are six-class diagnostic decoders, never streaming wake detectors.
No existing trained detector is loaded and no validation/final data are scored.
limits: Closed six-class, already known word-window diagnosis; no streaming detector/FAR or recognition acceptance.
All sources are existing synthetic training recordings, not independent real speakers.
Original auxiliary energy/synthesis anchors are retained and are not phonetic ground truth.
Poor ridge transfer cannot prove an intrinsic representation limit or faulty source pronunciation.
Excluded-engine results cannot choose detector thresholds, operating windows or a deployment candidate.
interpretation: Both representations exceed their label-permutation controls on this synthetic closed-class diagnostic, so these features support some cross-engine lexical decoding. Overall six-class macro hides a severe target-class transfer deficit: excluded Piper targets reach74/3000 with full history and265/3000 with time mean;2536/2593 are respectively assigned Hey Nick. Full-history target recall averaged equally across engines is65.20967%, versus52.03015% for the time mean. This is not a streaming detection result and does not isolate pronunciation, anchor, data-coverage or representation causes. Do not select a replacement or conclude that time averaging improves target detection from the six-class macro.
